:::{#thm-inverse-product}
#### Inverse of a product

If $\matr{A}$ and $\matr{B}$ are invertible $p \times p$ matrices,
then $\matr{A}\matr{B}$ is invertible, and

$$(\matr{A}\matr{B})^{-1} = \matr{B}^{-1}\matr{A}^{-1}$$

:::

::: proof

Multiply $\matr{A}\matr{B}$ by the candidate inverse on the right:

$$
\ba
(\matr{A}\matr{B})(\matr{B}^{-1}\matr{A}^{-1})
&= \matr{A}(\matr{B}\matr{B}^{-1})\matr{A}^{-1}
&& \text{(matrix multiplication is associative)}
\\
&= \matr{A}\,\matr{I}_p\,\matr{A}^{-1}
&& \text{(definition of } \matr{B}^{-1} \text{)}
\\
&= \matr{A}\matr{A}^{-1}
&& \text{(identity matrix)}
\\
&= \matr{I}_p
&& \text{(definition of } \matr{A}^{-1} \text{)}
\ea
$$

and on the left:

$$
\ba
(\matr{B}^{-1}\matr{A}^{-1})(\matr{A}\matr{B})
&= \matr{B}^{-1}(\matr{A}^{-1}\matr{A})\matr{B}
&& \text{(matrix multiplication is associative)}
\\
&= \matr{B}^{-1}\,\matr{I}_p\,\matr{B}
&& \text{(definition of } \matr{A}^{-1} \text{)}
\\
&= \matr{B}^{-1}\matr{B}
&& \text{(identity matrix)}
\\
&= \matr{I}_p
&& \text{(definition of } \matr{B}^{-1} \text{)}
\ea
$$

So $\matr{B}^{-1}\matr{A}^{-1}$ satisfies @def-matrix-inverse for $\matr{A}\matr{B}$.
The steps use @thm-matmul-assoc and @thm-identity.

:::
